pattern: Comparative structure: Just like A, B...
explanation: Used to draw a parallel between two similar situations. 'Just like' introduces a familiar scenario to explain an unfamiliar one.
explanationKo: 'Just like A, B...' 구조는 두 가지 비슷한 상황을 비교할 때 사용해요. 익숙한 상황을 먼저 제시해서 낯선 상황을 설명하는 표현이에요.
examples: Just like the U.S. doesn't want illegal immigration from Mexico, Mexico doesn't want illegal immigration from Guatemala.

explanation: Used to describe actions completed at an unspecified time that have present relevance. Emphasizes result or accomplishment rather than timing.
explanationKo: 현재완료(have/has + 과거분사)는 과거에 완료된 행동이 현재와 관련이 있을 때 사용해요. 시점보다 결과나 성취에 초점을 맞춰요.
examples: We've been able to do this.

pattern: Conditional: If + present simple, can/will + verb
explanation: Used to express a real or likely condition and its result. The 'if' clause sets up the condition, and the main clause describes the consequence.
explanationKo: 'If + 현재시제, can/will + 동사'는 실현 가능한 조건과 그 결과를 표현할 때 사용해요. 'if' 절이 조건을 세우고, 주절이 결과를 설명해요.
examples: If you don't pay, you may have to see an ad at the end of a lesson.
If you really want to deliver education to everyone, you have to make it accessible.

explanation: Used to introduce a contrasting fact or situation. It highlights the difference between two ideas within a single sentence.
explanationKo: 'Whereas'는 대조되는 사실이나 상황을 소개할 때 사용해요. 한 문장 안에서 두 가지 아이디어의 차이를 부각시켜요. '반면에'로 해석해요.
examples: Whereas with languages, if you were a waiter and you learned English, now you can be a waiter at a hotel.
When you're learning something, you get meaning out of it, whereas when you're scrolling for two hours on Instagram, you feel like you just wasted your time.

pattern: Not only A, but also B
explanation: Used to add emphasis by presenting two related ideas where the second is more important or surprising. Often used in persuasive speech.
explanationKo: 'Not only A, but also B'는 두 가지 관련된 아이디어를 제시하면서 두 번째를 더 강조할 때 사용해요. 설득적인 연설에서 자주 쓰여요.
examples: Not only do you have to make it accessible, but also you have to make it so that people want to actually learn.

pattern: It turns out that + clause (revealing information)
explanation: Used to introduce a surprising or previously unknown fact. It signals that what follows may contradict expectations.
explanationKo: 'It turns out that'은 놀라운 사실이나 이전에 몰랐던 정보를 소개할 때 사용해요. 뒤에 오는 내용이 예상과 다를 수 있음을 알려줘요.
examples: It turns out that the vast majority of the revenue for Duolingo comes from people who pay to subscribe.
It turns out that the algorithm for choosing what time to send you a notification is pretty simple.

explanation: Used to explain why something is the case. A direct and clear way to state a cause or justification.
explanationKo: 'The reason (for/that/why) is (that/because)...'는 이유를 설명할 때 사용해요. 원인이나 정당성을 직접적이고 명확하게 제시하는 방법이에요.
examples: The reason for that is because English can truly transform your life.
The reason people come back every day is because, well, if they don't come back, that number resets to zero.

explanation: Using a gerund (verb + -ing) as the subject of a sentence. This is common in formal and semi-formal English.
explanationKo: 동명사(동사 + -ing)를 문장의 주어로 사용하는 구조예요. 격식체와 반격식체 영어에서 흔히 사용돼요.
examples: Delivering education over a smartphone is like hoping that people will eat their broccoli.
Giving equal access to education to everyone.

explanation: Used to acknowledge a potential obstacle while maintaining that the main point still holds. Expresses resilience or determination.
explanationKo: 'Even if/though'는 장애물을 인정하면서도 주요 주장이 여전히 유효하다는 것을 보여줄 때 사용해요. '~하더라도'라는 의미예요.
examples: Even if you're not as engaging as those apps are, you can still get hundreds of millions of people to use your product.
Even though I didn't grow up rich.

explanation: Used to add essential information about a noun. Relative clauses with 'where', 'which', and 'that' modify nouns and provide more context.
explanationKo: 관계절(where/which/that)은 명사에 대한 필수적인 정보를 추가할 때 사용해요. 명사를 수식하면서 더 많은 맥락을 제공해요.
examples: A future in which screen time is not a bad thing.
Countries in which people are predominantly learning English.
